lines: Get DOWN! Nobody goes up there.
Something made of mud... that still knows the way down.
Prague, around 1600. The legend says the Jewish Town had enemies, and nobody to protect it.
So Rabbi Loew went down to the river... and shaped a giant out of clay.
He wrote a holy name on a slip of paper, and put it in the giant's mouth. It opened its eyes.
Every Friday before sunset, I take the word out. On the Sabbath, even you rest.
The golem guarded the streets all night. It fetched the water...
And every Friday, for years, the rabbi remembered.
The sun went down. The Sabbath song had already begun... and the word was still in its mouth.
It tore through the streets. Doors split. Carts flew. And it grew, with every step.
The rabbi ran out, mid-song. He reached up into its mouth, and pulled out the word.
The giant fell apart... into a pile of clay.
They carried the clay up to the attic. And took the stairs away.
In 1920, a reporter climbed up there. He found only dust.
Then why do they still sing that song twice? Every Friday.
